question.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation ${x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=6?$
question.worked_solution:
Consider the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.$ To determine the curve defined by the given equation, we reduce $Q(x)$ to its canonical (diagonal) form. 

First, we write down the matrix of $Q(x),$ which is

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we find the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

So, our quadratic form can be reduced to $2{y}_{1}^{2}.$ 

In the new variables, the given curve has the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}^{2} & =6 \\ {y}_{1}^{2} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

This represents the two parallel lines ${y}_{1}=\sqrt{3}$ and ${y}_{1}=-\sqrt{3}.$
